comment: The pipeline on the landing page. board lays out the stages and the files between them. Each stage shows its files (or, for a file an earlier stage wrote, that stage's output) and runs its commands in this directory. run.mjs runs them with sxml on PATH and writes what each prints to output/. Run it after changing anything here: node website/pipeline/run.mjs

stages.name: Invisible XML
stages.summary: `tree-sitter:parse` reads AGENTS.md as Markdown and returns its syntax tree as XML. An Invisible XML grammar turns each sentence under “Rules” into an element; a sentence the grammar does not know becomes `<unknown-rule>`.

stages.name: XSD
stages.summary: An XSD 1.1 schema says which rules exist and what their values are: a limit is a positive integer, a directory ends with a slash. A draft AGENTS.md with a rule nobody can check fails here, before any code is read.

stages.name: XPath
stages.summary: `tree-sitter:parse` parses TypeScript too, with line numbers. XPath 4.0 then asks the syntax tree what a code search can only guess: how many parameters each function takes, and which functions each line calls.

stages.name: XQuery
stages.summary: An XQuery 4.0 query checks every rule against every file under src/, listed with EXPath File, and records each violation with its file, its line and the rule it breaks.

stages.name: XSLT
stages.summary: An XSLT 4.0 stylesheet has one template rule per kind of rule and writes the violations as plain text for the agent. A hook runs the whole pipeline after each edit; when it finds a violation, the agent reads the message and fixes its change.

commands.note: exit status 2: Claude Code shows the agent this message
